heroHeadline: Ocean Cleanup Enters India with Mumbai Interceptors; Florida Coral Shows Early Bleaching 25% Near Miami
heroSubtitle: The Ocean Cleanup deployed Interceptor barriers at Mumbai's Trombay Creek and Malad Creek in late May 2026 — its first operations in India — targeting the estimated 5 million kg of plastic discharged annually by Mumbai waterways into the Arabian Sea. Scientists from the University of Miami's Rescue a Reef program reported on May 28 that approximately 25% of corals near PortMiami are already showing early bleaching signs, months ahead of the typical July–October bleaching season, as South Florida braces for another record-hot summer. TIME magazine simultaneously spotlighted coral biobanking and assisted-evolution laboratories in the UK and Germany racing to preserve coral genetic diversity for future reef restoration. A new wave of investors is entering blue economy conservation, with J.P. Morgan estimating the gross marine product at $2.5 trillion annually and ocean-climate startups having raised over $5 billion in venture funding over the past decade.
